name: Cantonese
variant: Cantonese of Hong Kong, traditional characters with Jyutping romanization
script: Chinese characters (traditional), taught with Jyutping (Latin letters and tone numbers 1–6); left to right
basis: Durham University Cantonese Beginners Steps 1-2 (係, 喺, 唔, question words, aspect markers, 嘅, then 有 / 冇, classifiers, prices, time, food, auxiliaries, comparison), with the Jyutping and tones opening of PolyU's Elementary Cantonese
src: Durham University, Cantonese Chinese language courses: summary of contents (Beginners Step 1 and 2, Elementary Step 1 and 2)
Hong Kong Polytechnic University, CBS1153 Elementary Cantonese (Taught in English) subject description, textbook: Chow Bun-Ching, Cantonese for Everyone (Jyutping version)
note: The grammar and topic order follows Durham Beginners Steps 1-2; the opening with Jyutping, syllable structure, tones and first characters follows PolyU. Neither source splits its content into lessons, so the split into 25 lessons is my own judgment. The aspect markers 咗 / 緊 / 過 are moved later than Durham's Step 1 so that verbs and time words come first; directions and 去 / 嚟 come from Durham's Elementary Step 2. Durham writes 有／無 and 唔洗; this roadmap uses the usual Hong Kong forms 冇 and 唔使.
hardest: Six tones (more if you count the checked syllables) that change meaning: 詩 si1, 史 si2, 試 si3, 時 si4, 市 si5, 事 si6
Characters: no link between how a character looks and how it sounds, and spoken Cantonese words with their own characters (係, 喺, 冇, 嘅)
Classifiers between every number or 呢 / 嗰 and the noun (一本書, 呢個人)
Sentence-final particles (呀, 啦, 喎, 㗎) that carry tone and attitude

items: Jyutping: initials and finals (ng-, gw-, aa against a, final -p -t -k)
Greetings and thanks: 你好 nei5 hou2, 早晨 zou2 san4, 唔該 m4 goi1 and 多謝 do1 ze6
First characters: strokes, stroke order and radicals (人 口 日 月 大 小)
係 hai6 (to be) and pronouns 我, 你, 佢, with 哋 for the plural
Introducing yourself: 我叫…, 我係美國人, 你叫咩名？
唔 m4: not; yes/no questions with 係唔係, 好唔好
Question words: 咩, 邊個, 邊度, 幾時, 點解
Numbers: 一 to 十, 百, 千, 萬
Classifiers: 個, 本, 杯, 張; 呢個 and 嗰個
喺 hai2: being at a place (我喺香港)
有 jau5 / 冇 mou5: have and there is
Money and prices: 幾多錢？, 蚊, 平啲
Ordering food and drink: 唔該, 要, 一杯奶茶, 埋單
Clock time and dates: 幾點？, 三點半, 星期一, 號
Want, can, like: 想, 可以, 識, 會, 鍾意, 要
Choices and 'also': A 定 B？ and 都
Describing and comparing: 好, 太, 幾, 啲, 咁

stages.en: Actions in time and getting around
items: 咗 zo2: completed actions, and 未 mei6 (not yet)
緊 gan2 and 過 gwo3: in progress and ever
去 and 嚟: going and coming; 搭車, 坐地鐵
Directions: 左邊, 右邊, 直行, 對面
Sentence-final particles: 呀, 啦, 吖, 呢
Suggestions and invitations: 不如…？, 一齊…吖
